Range of each channel's share across attribution rules

Source: R/attribute.R
attribution_spread.Rd

Summarises the output of attribute() into one row per channel, showing the range of its share of credited conversions across rules. A channel whose share swings from 8% to 31% depending on the convention has not been measured; it has been assigned a number.

Usage

attribution_spread(attribution)

Arguments

attribution

The data frame returned by attribute().

Value

A data frame with one row per channel, ordered by descending spread: channel, min_share, max_share, mean_share, spread (max_share minus min_share) and, only when both the "first" and "last" rules were run, first_last_ratio (the first-touch share divided by the last-touch share, NA when the last-touch share is 0). For a result of attribute(by = ), one row per segment and channel instead, with the segment columns first and rows ordered by segment, then by descending spread.

first_last_ratio here is a ratio of credited shares, which is not the same quantity as the column of the same name in channel_positions(), a ratio of touchpoint counts. They answer the same question in different currencies and will not agree numerically.

See also

attribute()

Examples

data(mm_events)
paths <- build_paths(mm_events, id = "customer_id", channel = "channel",
                     timestamp = "timestamp", conversion = "conversion")
attribution_spread(attribute(paths))
#>           channel  min_share  max_share mean_share       spread

#> 2     paid_search 0.09157242 0.27252827 0.18342704 0.1809558555

#> 5  organic_search 0.12623130 0.17876687 0.15470603 0.0525355710

#> 9          (none) 0.02736228 0.02982010 0.02849282 0.0024578273
